title: The work list
dek: What is being done here, as opposed to what is known.
lead: Every other register on this site answers what is **known** — [what has been read](/searched/), the [open questions](/open-questions/), [what cannot be closed](/gaps/), the [errands](/errands/) and the [corrections](/corrections/). None of them answered **what is being done**, so that lived in a chat window, which is the one place that does not survive the session. This is that list, in the shape the whole estate keeps it in. An item here names **who has to move it**, because an item with no owner is how a list becomes wallpaper.
close: Nothing is struck from this page when it turns out to be wrong; it is struck **through**, the same way a retracted claim is treated in [corrections](/corrections/). A list that quietly deletes its mistakes is telling you only what it wanted to be true.

rows.what: Read the regiment's book by hand — retired, not performed
rows.note: **Retired by the control rather than carried out, and the distinction is deliberate.** Images 652–662 were read (December 1787 to July 1791, no Llerena). Images 663–950 were **never read and now will not be**: the book is in the full-text index and Sancho is absent from it under all three spellings. **Done** is the nearest of the five states to what actually happened — the question this row existed to answer is answered, by cheaper means. **The caveat survives**: machine transcription of eighteenth-century hands is imperfect, so an index absence is weaker than a page absence, and if anything later contradicts this the 290 images are still there.

rows.what: Run the Berroeta control before reading another 290 images
rows.note: **Run and passed, 15 September 2026.** «Capellán del Regimiento Infantería de Buenos Ayres» returns **22 results** from a collection titled **Montevideo. Military Award Records 1812–1814**, with snippets reading «…de Berroeta Capellán del Regimiento…» and years **1789, 1790, 1791, 1792** — the chaplain and the exact years of the book. **The regiment's book is in the full-text index**, so the absence of any military collection from the 68 results for «Sancho Llerena» is evidence rather than a gap in coverage. Two limits kept open below.

rows.what: Finish harvesting the 68 full-text results for «Sancho Llerena»
rows.note: The sweep of 15 September returned **68 results** against far fewer in this archive's earlier attempts, and only about fifty titles and **three** snippets were actually read before the block returned. Results 51–68 were never displayed at all. Re-run at 100 per page, extract every ark, and resolve each through the tile service's manifest to a film and image — that route keeps working while the main site is blocked.

rows.what: Open two collections found in that sweep — both opened
rows.note: **Both opened.** **Montevideo Catedral, Baptism Records 1825–1828** at **dgs:007713376 images 515 and 601** — Francisco Juan Ramón (22 March 1826) and Lucinda Gregoria del Corazón de Jesús (12 May 1827), both grandchildren of Sancho through Dominga. **Cordón, Religious Marriage Records 1825–1916** at **dgs:007713391 image 1669** — Justa Pastora's marriage of 3 November 1830. **All three acts turned out to be already held**, which is what made the parent-pair query a coverage check rather than a discovery.

rows.what: Read DGS 7713375 — the Montevideo cathedral baptisms
rows.note: A film this archive had never named until 15 September. It holds the **1789 godparent act at image 551** and the **1811 baptism of Luis at image 2410** — the best document there is on Sancho's parents. Two images of it have been read and nothing else. It spans at least 1785 to 1811, which is the whole of Sancho's Montevideo life.

rows.what: Settle the Sánchez question — settled, against this session's own objection
rows.note: **Read at magnification: the castrense man is "Manuel Sánchez, Sargento de 1ª Clase del Regimiento, natural de la Ciudad de Córdova".** The Canelones petitioner is **"natural del Reino de Andalucía"**. **They do not match.** A man from the Andalusian city would be called **of Andalucía** — what the Canelones clerk writes, and what Sancho's own act means by **Córdova la Llana** — while an unqualified **la Ciudad de Córdova** in a Montevideo register most naturally means **Córdoba del Tucumán**, named in full a few leaves earlier in the same book. **So the objection this session raised against its own argument is withdrawn**, with the caveat that removing a counter-example is not producing evidence.

rows.what: Find the real Montevideo index, 1726–1800
rows.note: **DGS 7713386 is not it.** This archive called it «Índices de bautismos, matrimonios y defunciones, 1726–1800» and called opening it **the cheapest test in the archive**; images 300 and 1500 are cathedral burial registers of **1887 and 1905**. Two samples of 2,244 do not prove the index absent from that film, but the attribution is disproved and is logged in [corrections](/corrections/). The index may exist under another DGS — find it the way the Canelones one was found, from an image's own Information panel rather than from a catalogue line.

rows.what: Open a Córdoba parish register — the next country
rows.note: «Córdova la Llana» is the **city of Córdoba** in Andalusia; no municipality of that name exists because it is an epithet, and the qualifier distinguishes it from Córdoba del Tucumán. So Sancho was born there about 1767 and his parents **Félix Llerena and Rosalía Aguilar were natives of the same city**. **Nobody has yet looked at a single Córdoba parish register.** That is now the largest unopened door in this archive, and it is in Spain rather than Uruguay.

rows.what: Resolve Anton Armando Lerena — two records, deliberately not merged
rows.note: **Resolved 15 September 2026, and there was never a contradiction.** The J193 says Anton Armando Lerena died **3 April 2003**; estate 15127/2013 was advertised on **page 68** of the gazette of 16 August 2013. This archive's row held the **gazette year** and the **page number**, and this session read them as a death year and an age. gendatabase was right. One man. Logged in [corrections](/corrections/), along with the discovery that the whole column was mislabelled.

rows.what: Buy one South African death notice
rows.note: The 1994 death notice of **Ricardo Juan Carlos Lerena** (b. 1920, m. 1941 Doreen May Chappell) from gendatabase.com — the source David found, which this archive had never tried. A South African death notice **names the deceased's parents**, which would put in a modern official document what this archive currently infers: that the Cape Lerenas descend from Pablo Armando. **This session does not create accounts and does not pay for things**, so it stops here. Logged in [errands](/errands/).

rows.what: Settle whether five deaths in 1999 are a catastrophe or an artefact
rows.note: **Materially advanced 17 September 2026 without touching the paywall — data/1999-deaths-tested.tsv.** **The artefact reading is dead for three of the five.** The GEDCOM gives Pierre Frederick and both sons an exact shared day, 12 November 1999, and the Government Gazette — independent of it — advertised Pierre's estate ten weeks later. A default year does not behave that way. **Two of the five remain open and rest on a single index row each:** Gayle Lerena and Catherine Tertia Karon. **And one of those was never actually tested:** the gazette sweep was keyed on the surname **LERENA** and the index carries Catherine under **KARON**, so reporting her absence as a null would have been a straight error — sweep KARON too. Gayle's absence is doubly worthless: the Rhena May Lerena control shows this source misses real adult deaths, and a wife married in community of property shares one joint estate wound up in her husband's name, so the expected number of separate notices is exactly the one already found. **Still needs the death notices, and row 17 governs publication either way.** ** ANSWERED 20 September 2026: IT IS A CATASTROPHE, NOT AN ARTEFACT. ** The Johannesburg cemetery register — **free, and independent of the commercial index** — gives **Pierre Frederick and Richard both dead on 12 November 1999**, **Gayle and Jeffrey buried with them on 22 November**, and **all four sharing a burial registration of 18 November 1999** with **four consecutive record identifiers**: one family, entered in a single act of registration. **Gayle is the one the gazette could not reach**, and the refusal to publish her 1999 as fact was correct until now. **Doreen May died 17 November 1999**, five days after them. Only **Catherine Tertia Karon** remains untested, because she is indexed under **KARON**. ** AND THE FIFTH NAME IS NOW TESTED TOO. ** Catherine Tertia Karon was swept under **KARON**, the surname she is actually indexed under: **28 Karon records in South Africa** (so the surname is there), **281 Catherine Karons worldwide, every one American or Belgian**. **She is not found** — and she is **absent from the very Johannesburg register that holds the other four**. That is not proof she did not die in 1999; she may be buried in another province, and FamilySearch's South African civil death collection stops at **1967**. **But it is the first evidence pointing away from her being part of the same event, and it is recorded as a lean rather than a finding.**

rows.note: **Written up in notes/FOR-THE-ESTATE.md, 15 September 2026**, where a sibling session will find it, with working code and the traps spelled out. rows.what: Invent a register of outstanding work for this archive
rows.note: **Founded on a mistake and kept rather than deleted.** On 15 September this session was asked whether outstanding work was tracked centrally, found that it was not, and wrote data/open-threads.tsv — **the ninth session to invent its own answer**, which is precisely how this estate acquired a Chip meaning two things and one chart drawn under three names. The right thing already existed in the kit, written first in the Defranceschi archive. The content of that file has been folded into this list and the file retired. The lesson is the one the kit's own check states: a convention that lives in a document drifts, because nothing is checking it.

rows.what: Find Sancho Llerena's marriage act
rows.note: **Found 15 September 2026** after the archive had spent weeks recording it as probably not digitised. DGS 8166578, **image 2687** — «En ocho días del Mes de Enero de **1791** años… Sancho Llerena, natural de Córdova la Llana, hijo legítimo de **Félix Llerena** y de **Rosalía Aguilar**, naturales de dicha Córdova… con **María Fernández**, natural de las Asturias, hija legítima de **Rodrigo Fernández**». The year is in arabic numerals. It settles Córdoba against Granada, corroborates Apolant's date, confirms his parents independently of the 1811 baptism, and corrects the trees on the bride's father.

rows.what: Walk the Canelones informaciones matrimoniales
rows.note: **Finished 15 September 2026, with a negative.** DGS 8166573 does not cover January 1791: Volumen 6 runs to November 1790 and ends at image 1459, Volumen 7 opens at 1460 and its first dated case is March 1791. Sancho married on 8 January. The whole of 1791 in that series is one expediente belonging to somebody else. **A seam in the filing, not a failed search** — and the caveat is recorded: the filming card reads «hojas sueltas», so a stray sheet could sit elsewhere in Volumen 7. It also produced the one hard fact about the man himself: at image 2167 he is sworn as a witness and **could not sign his name**.

rows.what: Decide whether gendatabase-derived facts may stay on a public site
rows.note: **Materially reduced, 15 September 2026.** David chose to re-source rather than argue fair citation, and the South African Government Gazette — free and official — carried more than the index did. **The three sons of the 1950 estate are now off the commercial source entirely**: Ricardo Juan Carlos with exact dates, Nuno Fernando with exact dates and a wife nobody knew of, Rogue Luis Armando with his identity number. What is **still gendatabase's alone** is the later generation — Doreen May, Roberto Juan Roque, Brigitte Zaage, Anton Armando, Patricia MacEwan, Jeanette Riekstins, Belinda Michael, Paul Raymond, Rhena May, and the five deaths of 1999. Their gazette notices exist and are located but unread, so the decision is narrower than it was but not gone. **The attribution has still not been stripped.** ** MATERIALLY REDUCED AGAIN, 20 September 2026. ** The five 1999 deaths and Doreen May — the last facts in this archive that came only from the commercial index — are now carried by the **free Johannesburg cemetery register** with exact dates and record identifiers. **The decision this row asks for is now about very little.**

rows.what: Close the two limits on the Berroeta control
rows.note: **Both closed, 15 September 2026.** **Limit one:** six arks from the 22 results were resolved through the tile service's manifest — **five return DGS 7713373**, images 657, 667, 676, 716 and 831, and **image 657 is a page this session had already read by hand**. So the collection labelled **Military Award Records 1812–1814** is the regiment's book, whatever its label says. The sixth returns **DGS 7713382 image 2736**, the Montevideo marriage register. **Limit two:** all three spellings swept — «Sancho Llerena» 68, «Sancho Lerena» 143, «Sancho Lorena» — and **not one hit comes from DGS 7713373**.

rows.what: Finish the gazette re-sourcing — five estate notices already located
rows.note: **Four of the five done, and the fifth is a real null.** Read off the gazette: Anton Armando (b. 1952, d. 3 April 2003), Roberto Juan Roque (b. 20 March 1944, d. 20 February 2022), Brigitte (b. 16 October 1951, d. 18 May 2023), Belinda Maud (b. 16 January 1957, d. 2024 — the printed day is impossible and is flagged, not smoothed), and **Rogue Luis Armando in full: born 6 December 1905, died 29 January 1973**, which makes him the eldest of the three sons by fifteen years. **Doreen May could not be re-sourced**: her estate number returns only two J187s, neither carrying a date. Still open and moved to its own row. Also still unchased: the 1986 notice for **Lerena Racing Stables**, which belongs on [the horses page](/horses/).

rows.what: Find Doreen May Lerena's J193, and put Lerena Racing Stables on the horses page
rows.note: Two leftovers from the gazette work. **Doreen May** is the only person in this family who could not be taken off the commercial index: estate **16409/00** returns two J187 accounts and no J193, so gendatabase's **born 1921, died 1999** stands as **their** fact. Her notice may sit in an unindexed or badly scanned gazette of **2000**. And the **1986 notice for Lerena Racing Stables** (Government Gazette, 8 August 1986, no. 10383, page 7) has been located and never opened — it belongs beside the gazette's own description of Robert Paul Lerena as a **racehorse trainer**. ** DOREEN IS FREE-SOURCED, 20 September 2026. ** She was the last person in this family whose dates rested on the commercial index — **born 1921, died 1999** stood only as **their** fact. The Johannesburg cemetery register gives **died 17 November 1999, buried 20 November 1999** (ark 1:1:6NWQ-VLD4). **The J193 is no longer needed to get her off that index.** The Lerena Racing Stables half of this row is unaffected and still open.

rows.what: Map what is filmed and indexed for Córdoba and Asturias — done, and it changed the plan
rows.note: **Answered 15 September 2026, and the answer is two-sided.** **The bad half:** **Córdoba's parish registers are not on FamilySearch.** The Research Wiki's Church Records section for the province lists no FamilySearch collection at all — the registers are with the **Diocese of Córdoba**. Asturias is the same, with one partial exception (Spain, Diocese of **Santander**, Catholic Church Records 1538–1985 — contains some records for Asturias). Full text for Andalusia is nobility and notarial only. So Sancho's baptism is **not** sitting on a film waiting to be addressed by number; **that route is a letter to a diocesan archive, not a search**. **The good half, which corrects this session's own pessimism:** the provincial wiki pages are not the whole picture. A record search for Llerena in Spain 1730–1800 returns **228 results** from national collections the Córdoba page never mentions — **Spain, Catholic Church Records 1307–2005**; **Spain, Baptisms 1502–1940**; **Spain, Marriages 1565–1950**; and **Spain, Granada, Catholic Pre-Marriage Investigation Files, 1556–1899** — the same record type walked at Canelones this morning, indexed, for Andalusia, in the right century. **The eighteenth century is reachable by index even where it is not reachable by image.**

rows.what: Find Sancho Llerena's baptism, Córdoba, about 1767
rows.note: The single most valuable document not yet looked for. The act of 1791 puts his birth in the **city of Córdoba**; the trees say **about 1767** and that is still only a tree. A baptism would give the date, the parish, and his grandparents — **a fifth generation**, where this archive currently stops at four. Note the act gives no age, so 1767 is unverified and the search window should be generous, say 1760–1775.

rows.what: Find the marriage of Félix Llerena and Rosalía Aguilar, Córdoba, 1750s–60s
rows.note: The 1791 act says both were **naturales de dicha Córdova**, which is the first evidence placing the generation above Sancho anywhere at all. Their marriage act would give **their** parents and their own birthplaces. One tree claims Félix was born about 1725 and married about 1753, every value "about" and none sourced — treat it as a search hint, not a fact.

rows.what: Search Asturias for Rodrigo Fernández and Rosa Fernández
rows.note: **Never searched, in any form.** Two independent parish acts name them — the 1791 marriage and the 1811 baptism of their grandson Luis — and both say **naturales de las Asturias**. The 1791 act adds that they were **vecinos de Santa Lucía** in Uruguay, and the 1812 padrón puts Rodrigo, 63, **asturiano**, living in Sancho's own household. So they emigrated and lived with the family: their Asturian parish is findable and would carry María Fernández's baptism too.

rows.what: Test the Llerena–Aguilar compound in Spanish records — run, and it argues against hidalguía
rows.note: **Run 15 September 2026.** «Llerena y de Rosalía Aguilar» returns **zero**; «Félix Llerena» returns only modern Latin America; «Rosalía Aguilar» returns forty collections of which **two** are in Spain, both Jaén notarial of 1829–37. On its own that would be worthless — **so the control was run first.** The corpus that **is** indexed for Andalusia is **nobility and hidalguía files, chivalric orders and Madrid protocols**, searchable back to 1489 — exactly where an armigerous couple would appear. They do not. **Weak evidence that Félix and Rosalía were not gentry with a Chancillería file**, which sits with the 1811 act calling Sancho **Don** while the 1798 deposition says he could not write his name.

rows.what: Find Sancho Llerena's death
rows.note: **Searched 15 September 2026; a controlled null.** No indexed death or burial exists for him in Uruguay under any spelling — across 401 loose results he appears only as **father**, **father of the bride**, **spouse** or **other**, **never as the principal of a death**. **The control passed**: a surname-Rodríguez search for Montevideo deaths 1828–1838 returns church burials from **Nuestra Señora del Carmen, Cordón** — the exact parish where Justa Pastora married in 1830 and where Dominga lived — dated 1832, 1833 and 1838. So burials in his family's own parish, in the decade he is supposed to have died, **are** indexed, and he is not among them. **What that does not mean**: the index is name-based and a mangled surname is invisible to it, and the Cordón is one parish of several. He is not in the index; that is not the same as not in the registers. **The trees' 1832 remains a tree.**

rows.what: Find María Fernández's death
rows.note: **Same search, same control, same result.** No indexed death or burial for María Fernández, wife of Sancho Llerena, in Uruguay 1810–1870. She returns only in records already held. **One gain**: FamilySearch's index gives her **Parents Rosa Fernández, Rodrigo Fernández** — **a third independent witness** to what the 1811 baptism and the 1791 marriage act both say. Three sources, one couple, no disagreement.

rows.what: Build the complete list of Sancho and María's children from the registers
rows.note: The archive has them piecemeal — Pedro Antonio 1793, Agustina Ramona 1795, Fidel about 1799, Justa Pastora 1800, José Loreto 1806, Luis 1811 and others — assembled from scattered searches rather than from a systematic read. **Canelones baptisms 1791–1815 are filmed and the images are now addressable.** Reading them straight through would produce a closed sibling list instead of an open one, and the consistency checker already reports that its sibling tests reach only 106 of 277 people.

rows.what: Take Pedro Antonio Lerena forward from 1793
rows.note: **Traced.** His marriage was already held — **Vicenta Vega, natural de Cerro Largo, daughter of Don Romualdo and Doña Andrea Maestre** — but **his children were not**: the indexes give **Manuel Antonio** and **Vicenta Margarita**, and a **Pedro Antonio Natalio baptised at the Cordón on 12 December 1828**, born 1 December. One entry names his mother as **María Fernández**, consistent with him being Sancho's son; another garbles his father as **Francisco Llorena**, which is why these are recorded as candidates and not attached to the line.

rows.what: Read the 1812 padrón from the image, not from a transcript
rows.note: The archive quotes it — Sancho, **andaluz**, 45; María Fernández, 36; Rodrigo Fernández, 63, **asturiano**, in the household — but from a published transcription. Now that images are addressable by number, **read the entry itself**: padrones often carry occupation, household composition and enslaved people in columns transcriptions drop. Sancho's age of 45 in 1812 implies birth about 1767, which is currently the only support for that year. ** READ 20 September 2026, and the row's premise was wrong in the archive's favour. ** The page is **on FamilySearch**, in a collection nobody here had opened — **Uruguay, Census Records, 1726–1858** — so it could have been read from a desk at any point. Index ark **1:1:61LW-R54J** ('Sancho Llerena, masculino, 45, Andaluzia'), image ark **3:1:3QS7-99ZR-NKNR**. **The transcription was good:** Sancho, María Fernández and all six children read exactly as quoted. **What it did not carry:** four named people directly above him under household 59 — **Juana 41, Juan 'negro esclavo', Gabriel, María** — one explicitly enslaved, and **Juana is the name of the enslaved woman the 1812 baptism places in Sancho's household.** **Whose household those four are in is NOT resolvable at this resolution** and is not asserted. See the new row.

rows.what: Reclaim the errands that are now machine work — and the premise was wrong
rows.note: **The row assumed eleven errands sat on David. They did not — all eleven were already owned by me, this archive.** That is the third time today this session asserted something about its own files without checking them. **But it exposed a real fault underneath**: by the estate's own division — **errands.tsv is work for a person, the work list is work for a session** — eleven rows of the archive's own machine work were sitting in the wrong register. **All eleven migrated**: closed in errands.tsv with their detail kept verbatim, and seven new work-list rows opened for the ones that had no counterpart. What remains in errands is what it should be — institutions written to, and four things genuinely waiting on David. **Postscript: the migration was too blunt and drift.py refused it.** Setting all eleven to **done** claimed work was finished because its index entry had moved — and one of them says in its own detail that the register **has never been turned**. All eleven are back at **ready**, each now carrying a pointer to the work list, which is where their state is maintained. **The checker was right and the migration was wrong.**

rows.what: Find the DGS for the Montevideo marriage-dispensation register, 1856–1932
rows.note: Logged as an errand for David when catalogue search was returning **Something Went Wrong** all day. The route that works now: open any image from the right parish and read its **Information panel**, which prints the catalogue link and that reel's item-by-item contents. The archive already holds one dispensation from this series — the 1911 Lerena–Cardozo — so an anchor exists. ** ANSWERED 17 September 2026, sideways. ** A full-text search aimed at the parents' names returned a hit inside this very register, and the viewer's own header gives it: **DGS 007713367, item 13, 247 images**. Found while looking for something else and not found by searching the catalogue, which was still erroring.

rows.what: Search the Iglesia del Cordón, Montevideo
rows.note: Full text has already shown this archive two Cordón collections it has never opened — **Baptism Records 1828–1836** and **Religious Marriage Records 1825–1916**. The Cordón is where the Montevideo branch surfaces in the 1830s, and the 1831 Rivera godfather act sits there. Fold the errand into that work rather than leaving it addressed to David.

rows.what: Place Catherine Mary Sophia Lerena, born 25 March 1929
rows.note: **A wholly new person, produced this afternoon by the gazette**: the surviving spouse of Nuno Fernando Lerena, who died 1 July 1971 at 24 Leiden Road, Gerdview, Germiston. Nobody in this archive knew he was married. Her identity number is partly legible in the notice; her own estate, if she has one, would be findable on gazettes.africa and would name children — **grandchildren of Pablo Armando nobody has counted**.

rows.what: Ask where Rogue Luis Armando was born in 1905
rows.note: Directly tests one of this archive's declared [gaps](/gaps/) — **the eight years between Northam and the Cape**. Pablo Armando was born at Rosario in **1882**; his eldest son was born **6 December 1905**. If that birth was not in South Africa it locates the family in those missing years, and **Argentina is the obvious first place to look** — the archive already has Argentine baptism sweeps to extend. ** SHARPENED 20 September 2026, and the register's own answer is an inference. ** Roque was **baptised 12 June 1911 at Corpus Christi, Wynberg — aged five and a half, and three months before his parents married on 3 September 1911**, with his mother entered as **Mary Septima olim Taylor**. **So 'Cape Town' as his birthplace is taken from where he was baptised six years later, not from anything that states where he was born.** The pattern is legitimation. The question is still open and is now better posed.

rows.what: Find out who Rose Lilian Theys was
rows.note: The 1950 estate makes her **Executrix Testamentary**, gives her **a half-share of the residue**, and describes her as **"no relation"** — while listing her address as **No. 7 Forth Road, Newlands**, the same address as the deceased. A woman who is not a relative, lives with him, administers his estate and inherits a quarter of it is not a minor figure. gazettes.africa and the deceased-estates index will both carry her.

rows.what: Sweep gazettes.africa for TAYLOR and BOOYZEN
rows.note: The gazette pipeline works and cost nothing; it has so far been pointed only at **Lerena**. The other two South African lines in this archive are **Mary Septima Taylor**, Pablo Armando's wife, and the **Booyzens** who appear in the DNA as Cape Afrikaners. Estate notices would give both families exact dates and surviving spouses. **Search surname-first** — modern notices print **LERENA, Anton Armando**, not the other way round.

rows.what: Pull the Rapeport Incorporated thread
rows.note: One firm at **107 Oxford Road, Rosebank** acted for Doreen May in 2001, Anton Armando in 2013, Roberto Juan Roque in 2022 and Belinda Maud in 2024 — **a quarter-century of one family's estates**. That is not a coincidence and it is a way of establishing which Lerenas belong to this family without guesswork. It is also a live firm, which makes it a David question rather than a search, if it comes to contact.

rows.what: Make the build catch a stale errand
rows.note: **Done — tools/check-errands.py, wired into verify.sh.** It fails the build when an errand whose status is still open carries a detail that announces the errand is finished. **It found a false positive on its very first run** — an errand saying the work **"cannot be closed online at all"**, which is about feasibility, not about the errand — so the patterns were tightened to phrases that can only mean **this errand is over**. A bare **closed** is useless here, and **a noisy check gets switched off**. Then proved both ways: planting the real case (the 1791 marriage errand set back to **ready**) makes it exit 1 and name the row; restoring it returns to green. **40 errands checked, none finished-but-open.**

rows.what: Audit this archive's other catalogue-derived film numbers
rows.note: Distinct from the estate-wide warning below it. **Two of two Montevideo attributions failed inspection today** — DGS 7713373 was mislabelled but right, DGS 7713386 was simply wrong. Every other DGS in this archive that came from reading a catalogue rather than opening the film is now suspect. They are cheap to test: one manifest.json call resolves any image to its true film and image number. ** AUDITED 20 September 2026 - see /method/ and data/dgs-audit.tsv. ** **All 58 DGS numbers tested at three images each. 57 resolve; 0 not found.** The suspicion is cleared. Done **with FamilySearch signed out**, because thumb_p200.jpg is public — and note a correction to this archive's own method note: **manifest.json is not public**, it answers 401 to an anonymous request. Two traps recorded, both of which would have produced false corrections: **401 means a restricted image, not a wrong film** (one film gives 401 at image 1 and 200 at image 100), and a first pass that matched **film** as well as **DGS** threw six false failures that are **old microfilm roll numbers, correctly labelled**. One open item: **DGS 008166571** gave no 200 anywhere, so it is restricted rather than proven.

rows.what: Check the living-person gate — the tick was assumed, and now it is asked

rows.what: Give every person a last-attested-alive date
rows.note: The Sancho search exposed a gap in the archive's own shape: it records when a person is **named**, not when they were last **demonstrably alive**. A man named as a grandfather may have been twenty years dead. **One field, computed where possible from the record type**, would stop that confusion for 278 people rather than one. ** BUILT 20 September 2026 - tools/last-alive.py, rendered on /register/. ** **Computed, never typed, and it does not guess** — dates in this archive live in prose, and prose carries other people's dates too. rows.what: The nine Taylor children followed to their deaths — eight of nine, and four married surnames recovered
rows.note: ** PART DONE the same evening it was written, 16 September 2026. ** The three 1900 deaths were run and ** all three are in the index, all three in BIDEFORD, all within nine months of each other: ** **Georgina Brayley, age 85, Mar quarter, 5b/421** — the Scotswoman, and ** 85 is exactly right for a birth of 23 August 1814 at Haddington **; **Mary Ann H Taylor, age 56, Jun quarter, 5b/363**; and **John Walker Brayley, age 53, Dec quarter, 5b/305**. ** His age is the one thing tonight that did NOT match ** — 53 at 22 October 1900 means born about 1847, and the tree says 22 June 1845. ** Two years out, in a family whose other two ages were exact to the month **, which points at the tree rather than the informant. ** And neither he nor his sister has a registered birth at all ** — no John Walker Brayley 1843–1850 anywhere, no Mary Brayley or Brailey in Jun 1843. ** That is a household that did not register births **, which was lawful before 1875 — so the place to look is the **parish baptism register**, which is where "St Paul's" and "St Bartholomew's" pointed all along. ** THEN THE NINE TAYLOR CHILDREN, IN ONE SEARCH — births, surname Taylor, Bideford district, 1870–1890. ** ** NINE OF NINE, every one in the right quarter **, including **Mary Septima, Dec quarter 1884, 5b/506** — ** Pablo Armando's wife now has her own birth registration. ** The tree's odd-looking pair of November 1870 births turns out to be right: both registered that quarter on adjacent pages, 489 and 490, so they are twins. ** But the names are the find, not the dates: Isabella TEMPLE (1874), Margaret Hellen W[ALKER] (1876) and Agnes WALKER (1889). ** Those are the surnames of Georgina Temple and of **Helen Walker**, who five generations up cited **nothing at all**. ** She is still not on a record — but three of her descendants were registered with her surname by a clerk, and that is. ** ** AND A THIRD SPELLING TRAP, LOGGED BECAUSE IT NEARLY LANDED. ** A county-wide search of all 129 Brayleys in FreeCEN's Devon for 1861 found none of this family, ** with a clean control ** — 53 Taylors at Bideford the same year. It was one sentence away from being recorded as "the family left Bideford between 1851 and 1870". ** Searched again as BRAILEY, every one of them came back, on the same street as in 1851. ** ** A controlled null is only ever as good as the spelling it was run under. ** ** FOURTH PASS, 17 September 2026 — the sibling DEATHS, which were the unfinished half. ** ** HORACE ARCHIBALD: Deaths, March quarter 1934 — TAYLOR, Horace A, AGE 61, BIRMINGHAM. ** A death on 18 January falls in the March quarter and a man born April 1872 is exactly 61 that January. ** The district is the surprise — Birmingham, not Devon — but he was a FOOTMAN at nineteen in 1891, and servants went where the places were. ** ** WILLIAM JOHN, the twin: Deaths, June quarter 1951 — TAYLOR, William J, AGE 80, TOTNES. ** Quarter, age, initial and county all right. ** Of the twins born in one quarter of 1870, one died in Devon at eighty and the other went to Cape Town. ** ** AND A METHOD RULE THAT NEARLY COST BOTH: the first search for each man returned NOTHING. ** "Horace Archibald" and "William John" both give no rows; both men are there under **Horace A** and **William J**. ** The GRO index abbreviates second forenames, so a FULL-forename search is WEAKER than a first-forename one. Search the first forename and filter by AGE. ** Controls held both times — 34 Horace Taylors in the decade, 205 William Taylors in 1951 at >99%. ** The coverage was never the problem; the query was. ** ** AND THE SISTERS, 17 September — which needed a different method and cracked two of them. ** A married woman vanishes from the death index under her maiden name and this archive holds no husbands. That looked like a wall; ** it is not, because the MARRIAGE index still holds her maiden name. ** **KATHLEEN GEORGINA** — never married: Taylor, Kathleen G, age 69, Mar q 1940, **Bideford**. Born and died in the same town. **ISABELLA TEMPLE** — married Sep q 1900 at Bideford, 5b/901, a page carrying four names, so the index could not say which man was hers. ** Her death settles it: DALLING, Isabella T, age 79, Dec q 1953, Bideford. She married HENRY DALLING ** — disambiguated by her own death fifty-three years later. **LUCY ELIZABETH** — married Jun q 1909 at **Totnes**, 5b/373, a page carrying **only two names**: **William Norrish SWEET** and herself. Died **Sweet, Lucy E, age 75, Jun q 1957, Plymouth**. ** Two husbands and two married surnames the archive did not have. And Totnes is not random — her brother William John died at Totnes in 1951. ** ** THE METHOD, for Irene, Margaret Hellen Walker and Agnes: ** death under Taylor → if absent, **that is a finding**; marriage under Taylor → take vol/page → search the page with no surname → the husband appears → death under his surname, confirmed on **age**. If the page holds four names, the death resolves the pairing. ** COMPLETED 17 September 2026. EIGHT OF THE NINE now have a marriage, a death, or both. ** **Irene → Henry Albert BURTON** (Bideford 1900, 5b/900; d. Barnstaple 1969, aged 90). **Agnes Walker → Alfred S WOOD** (Devonport 1918, 5b/588; d. Cheltenham 1974, **date of birth 3 August 1889** — her birthday to the day). **Margaret Hellen Walker** married at **St Pancras**, Dec q 1903, 1b/43 — ** husband unresolved, either Charles William Bell or Arthur Wallis, and with no death date there is nothing to disambiguate on. ** ** And a detail only visible with the pages side by side: IRENE MARRIED ON 5b/900 AND ISABELLA ON 5b/901 — adjacent pages, same quarter, same district. Two sisters married at Bideford within days of each other in autumn 1900, the year their mother died. ** ** FOUR RULES ABOUT THIS INDEX ARE NOW IN brayley-bmd.tsv: ** search the first forename only; a woman missing from the death index has married and the MARRIAGE index still holds her maiden name; when a marriage page holds four names the DEATH resolves the pairing; and the index changes shape twice — **from 1912 it names the spouse**, **from ~1969 it gives a date of birth instead of an age**.

rows.what: The 1891 census at Northam — done. The household is found, and two children are missing from it
rows.note: ** DONE the same evening it was opened, 16 September 2026, and it gave more than it was asked for. ** FreeCEN holds Northam for 1891. ** The household is at 2 FORE STREET, NORTHAM ** — piece 1787, ED 4, folio 42, page 1, schedule 2. See data/1891-northam-census.tsv. ** WILLIAM TAYLOR, head, 65, "Cab Driver / ret'd Army Srgt", born Worlingworth, Suffolk ** — which also solves a puzzle filed as a data error: the tree attaches "Sergeant-Major in the army" to the infant who died at nine months in 1825, and ** the trade belongs to this man, on a census return, in his own house. ** ** MARY A. H. TAYLOR, wife, 47, born ST BARTHOLOMEWS, LONDON (CITY) ** — and that is the birthplace FreeBMD could not find a registration for. ** Three independent records now agree on 1843 and not one of them is her birth certificate. ** ** WILLIAM J. and KATHLEEN G., both 20, both born Bideford: the twins are confirmed ** for the third time. ** WHAT IT DID NOT SETTLE: ** there is no Edith, so that candidate is weakened — ** but MARY SEPTIMA, aged 6, is missing from her own parents' household too **, and a county-wide check of all 368 Devon Taylors born 1882–1886 does not find her. ** A census cannot tell a child who was elsewhere from a child who never was **, and a child who died before 1891 would fit every fact. ** The count still demands a seventh daughter. Row 128. ** ** MARKED DONE 20 September 2026 — it had been finished for four days and left open. ** The census work is complete and the one question it could not settle, the seventh daughter, **is row 128's and is already written there**. A row whose remainder lives in another row is finished, not open.

rows.what: The tenth Taylor child — FreeBMD cannot settle it; ONE GRO search can
rows.note: ** Two questions that did not exist this morning, both raised by records rather than by trees. ** **(1)** Mary Septima Taylor, born Northam, registered Dec quarter 1884, ** is not in her parents' house at 2 Fore Street on 5 April 1891 **, and is not among the 368 Taylors born 1882–1886 in FreeCEN's Devon. ** The null is soft ** — FreeCEN's Devon 1891 is transcribed parish by parish and is not complete — ** but Northam itself IS complete, which is what makes her absence from it real. ** Her elder sister Isabella Temple, 16, is absent too, and at that age service explains it; ** at six it does not. ** **(2)** The tree says ten children and names nine, and ** SEPTIMA MEANS SEVENTH ** while the known daughters make her sixth. ** THE CHEAPEST TEST OF BOTH: the 1901 census at Northam **, where she would be 16 — FreeCEN's place list should be checked for Northam 1901. ** And for the tenth child, FreeBMD deaths in the Bideford district 1871–1890 under an infant age **, because a child who died before 1891 would be in the birth index, counted among the ten, and in no census at all. ** UPDATE, SAME EVENING. ** The first suggestion above is dead: ** FreeCEN lists Northam for 1851, 1861 and 1891 only, so there is no 1901 there. ** But the same place list held **Westleigh for 1851**, and chasing that instead found ** the whole family at LOWER GUNSTONE, BIDEFORD on 30 March 1851 ** — see data/1851-bideford-brayley.tsv. ** It answered three other open questions and raised one new person. ** John Walker Brayley is aged 5 there, which fits the tree's 1845 and ** not ** the 1900 death index's implied 1847, so that discrepancy resolves in the tree's favour; Georgina Margaret Brayley is ** 8 months old, so born about July 1850, and the tree's "1851" is a year late **; and there is ** an ISABELLA BRAYLEY, 10, born London (St Andrew), whom this archive did not have at all. ** ** The two questions in this row are still open. ** ** SECOND UPDATE. The obvious hypothesis was tested and it FAILS. ** Georgina Temple was alive and in Northam in 1891 — found only by searching BRAYLEY, the fourth spelling trap of the evening — ** and she is ALONE in the ALMS HOUSE ** (piece 1787, ED 6, folio 72, schedule 40), "Living On Means", aged 77. ** Mary Septima was not with her grandmother. ** She is not at 2 Fore Street, not in the alms house, and not among the 368 Devon Taylors born 1882–1886. ** Where she was at six years old is a real open question.** ** WORKED 17 September 2026 AND HANDED OVER, because it is structurally beyond this session. ** The infant-death search this row asked for was run: **FreeBMD deaths, Taylor, Bideford district, 1881–1891 — 37 entries, fourteen of them aged 0–3.** ** An ETHEL Taylor, born Bideford Dec quarter 1882, died aged two, fits the gap exactly ** — born between Lucy Elizabeth and Mary Septima, dead before any census could hold her. ** And she cannot be attached to this family, and neither can Edith, and neither can the other five infant girls. ** ** THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL: the FreeBMD birth index carries NO mother's maiden name and the death index carries NO parents, so there is no field anywhere in FreeBMD capable of joining a Bideford Taylor child to THIS household. ** More searching there will not help. ** WHAT SETTLES IT IN ONE SEARCH, AND IT IS YOURS: the GRO's own index at gro.gov.uk is NOT FreeBMD and gives the MOTHER'S MAIDEN NAME on every birth from 1837. ** Search **births, surname TAYLOR, mother's maiden name BRAYLEY, district BIDEFORD, 1870–1890**. ** That returns every child of William Taylor and Mary Ann Hellen Brayley by definition, with no inference at all — the tenth included, whoever she was. ** It needs a free GRO account, which this session does not create. ** The second half of the row — where Mary Septima was at six in 1891 — remains open and is not answerable from FreeCEN, whose Devon 1891 is transcribed parish by parish. **

rows.what: Isabella Brailey — she vanishes after 1861, and the silence is controlled
rows.note: ** Found on the 1851 census at Lower Gunstone, Bideford: BRAYLEY, Isabella, granddaughter, 10, born London (City), ST ANDREW ** — an elder sister of Mary Ann Hellen Brayley, born about 1841, ** who appears nowhere in the current tree. ** ** She is worth chasing for two reasons beyond simply being a person. ** **(1)** ** Mary Ann Hellen named her second daughter ISABELLA TEMPLE ** — registered at Bideford, December quarter 1874 — ** so she named a child for this sister and gave her their mother's maiden name too. ** **(2)** ** Sue Rowbotham's family history has a chapter called "The mystery of the missing husband and daughter". ** The missing husband is now firmly John Brailey, alive in the asylum on census night and dead five weeks later. ** Whether Isabella is the missing daughter is NOT established and is written here only so it can be tested, not assumed. ** Where to look: FreeBMD births, Brayley or Brailey, London, 1840–1842 — St Andrew Holborn is the likely parish; then her marriage or death. ** UPDATE, SAME EVENING: SHE IS CONFIRMED. ** The 1861 census at Lower Gunstone, Bideford has **BRAILEY, Isabella, daughter, unmarried, 20, NEEDLE WOMAN, born London (City), St Andrews** — ** the same birthplace as 1851, ten years apart, so she is a real person and not a transcription ghost. ** See data/1861-bideford-brailey.tsv. ** What is still open is what became of her: ** a marriage or a death, and whether she is Sue Rowbotham's missing daughter — ** which remains untested and must not be assumed. ** ** ANSWERED 17 September 2026, and the answer is a controlled silence. ** No marriage under **Brailey or Brayley** in Devon 1861–1890; **none anywhere in England and Wales 1858–1895**; and **no death** under either spelling 1861–1925. ** Control: Brayley marriages with no forename in 1870 alone return FOURTEEN nationally ** — the surname is thickly indexed and the searches could have found her. ** She did not marry in England and did not die in England. ** Either she emigrated, or she married or died under one of this surname's manglings. ** And a candidate, offered as a candidate: ** of John Brailey and Georgina Temple's four children, Mary Ann Hellen, John Walker and Georgina Margaret all have documented later lives. ** Isabella alone has nothing after 1861, which makes her the best candidate for Sue Rowbotham's "missing daughter" — an argument from absence, the weakest kind, and recorded as untested. ** See data/brayley-two-questions.tsv.

rows.what: Georgina Brayley of Kilburn — REFUTED, and the search that refuted her found his marriage
rows.note: ** Found in the 1891 census at Tower Street, Northam ** — piece 1787, ED 3, folio 36, schedule 107 — **BRAYLEY, Georgina, servant, single, 20, General Servant, born Middlesex, LONDON KILBURN**, in the household of Thomas Lock, draper. ** The pattern is the family's exactly: ** Mary Ann Hellen herself was a "House Servant" in a china dealer's house at Bideford at eighteen. ** And the forename is the family's ** — Georgina Temple's name is carried by Georgina Margaret (1850) and Kathleen Georgina (1870). ** The obvious reading is a granddaughter of Georgina Temple, most likely a daughter of JOHN WALKER BRAYLEY ** , who was born in London, was 26 in 1871, and whose birthplace the records give as St Pancras. ** NONE OF IT IS PROVEN. The census states no relationship to anybody in this family. ** What would settle it: her birth in the index, London, about 1871, under Brayley or Brailey; and whether John Walker Brayley married at all — ** the archive has no marriage for him, and he died at Bideford in 1900. ** ** REFUTED 17 September 2026. ** **John Walker Brayley married in the December quarter of 1876, at Bideford, 5b/978** — ** five years AFTER a child born at Kilburn in 1871. ** She cannot be his daughter by that marriage. ** The reasoning that produced her — a Brayley of the right age, in service at Northam, carrying the family's forename — was a resemblance and nothing more, and she is not adopted. ** ** What the same search bought: ** page 5b/978 carries **Bonning Elizabeth, Brayley John Walker, Paddon Elizabeth, Richards John** — two marriages. ** So John Walker married an ELIZABETH, either Bonning or Paddon **, and the index cannot say which, exactly as on his sister's 5b/794 six years before. The certificate would settle it and would name his father.

rows.what: Piedmont: mapped in detail, and the Turin route cannot close it — the Argentine end can
rows.note: ** Opened 16 September 2026 out of David's question, "do we have a Juan Carlos Lerena / Lerina in Italian records?" ** ** The direct answer is no ** — no Giovanni Carlo or Gian Carlo under either spelling, controlled. ** The useful answer is that LERENA and LERINA are Italian surnames and they sit in PIEDMONT: ** 66 exact Lerena records in Italy clustered in the **Diocese of Torino**, and **114** exact Lerina, Torino again plus **Ivrea**. See data/italy-lerena-lerina.tsv. ** And that is the same corner the DNA points at. ** The archive's own DNA page reasons that Cheryl's **11.1% Italian**, with three non-Italian grandparents, implies **about 44% in Pablo Armando — one Italian parent** — and that the split is ** NORTHERN-dominant, 6.1 against 3.6. ** ** Two independent things, an admixture estimate and a surname distribution, now point at northern Italy, and neither of them names anybody. ** ** WHAT TO DO WITH IT: ** the Torino and Ivrea civil registration and diocesan records are indexed on FamilySearch and are searchable by parent name — ** so look for a LERINA or LERENA male born about 1840–1862 in Piedmont who then DISAPPEARS from the Italian record **, and cross him against the Argentine arrivals. The archive already holds cemla-lerina.tsv: a **Lerina family of four landing at Buenos Aires from GENOVA on 15 March 1889** — ** seven years too late to be his parents arriving, but the right surname on the right route **, and Genova is the port Piedmont emigrates through. ** Also worth re-running CEMLA for LERENA and LERINA before 1882, which is the arrival that would matter. ** ** ANTENATI CHECKED, 16 September 2026, and it cannot answer this. ** The Italian State Archives' own portal returns **one** Lerena in its whole national name index — ** Cesare Lerena, death 1915, BRESCIA ** — and eight Lerina, most of them the different surname **Di Lerina**. ** The control destroys that null: ** Antenati holds **2,621 registers for Torino**, but a name search there for ROSSI restricted to Torino returns 102 people called ** Charles, Marguerite and Jacinte, in 1805–1811 ** — ** the Torino name index is NAPOLEONIC ONLY, kept in French, and does not reach the 1840s–1880s at all. ** ** So Antenati's images exist for Piedmont and are not name-searchable for the years that matter ** — the same lesson as the Rosario typescript and the FreeREG Devon parishes, that the null belongs to the finding aid and not to the past. ** The searchable collection for the right years is FamilySearch's "Italy, Torino, Torino, Civil Registration (Tribunale), 1866-1899" **, which is where the 66 and 114 came from. Antenati's 2,621 Torino registers are the fallback: browsable by comune and year, image by image, the way Rosario and Canelones were read. ** WORKED IN DETAIL 16 September 2026, and the conclusion is negative in a useful way. ** **49 Lerina records in and around Torino** — Ivrea, Montaldo Roero, Costigliole — ** families that stay put for sixty years **, with two Carlo Lerinas acting as fathers and neither a candidate for anything. ** THE ROUTE IS STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE of answering the question: ** the Turin civil series begins in **1866**, so a man born in the 1840s–50s has no birth record in it at all; and ** an emigrant leaves no later Italian record by construction **, so "a son who vanishes" cannot be told from an unindexed death or a move. ** Enumerating Piedmontese Lerinas maps the people who STAYED, which is the complement of what is wanted. ** ** Do not spend a week on it. **

So it is yours. ** SETTLE THE COVERAGE FIRST, because it may make the whole search pointless. ** The earliest arrival this archive holds under **any** spelling is the Lerina family of **15 March 1889**, from Genova. ** CEMLA's arrivals database is generally given as beginning in 1882 ** — and if that is right, then an arrival before **February 1882**, which is the only one that could carry Pablo Armando's parents into the country before his birth, ** is invisible to it by construction, and finding nothing would prove nothing. ** ** IF IT DOES REACH BACK FURTHER, the searches are: ** LERENA, LERINA, LARENA and LORENA, arrivals before 1882, and note the **port** — ** Genova is how Piedmont emigrates **, and Piedmont is where both the surname and the northern-Italian DNA now point (row 134, data/italy-lerena-lerina.tsv).

rows.what: When he left Argentina — nothing dates it, and one prop has been knocked away
rows.note: ** REWRITTEN the same day it was opened, because the control demoted half of it. ** ** THE STRONG HALF STANDS: there was no LERENA and no LERINA household, under any spelling, anywhere in SANTA FE PROVINCE in the 1895 National Census. ** Controlled: a Gonzalez search returns **88,739** records with the 1895 census reaching San Cristóbal, **Alberdi/Rosario**, San Jerónimo and Iriondo, so the index is dense and covers Rosario itself. ** For a whole surname to be absent from a province indexed that thickly, it has to be genuinely absent ** — and that agrees with the Rosario baptism sweep from an entirely different record type. ** THE WEAK HALF IS WITHDRAWN AS EVIDENCE. ** This archive said earlier today that Pablo Armando's own absence from the 1895 census at thirteen suggested he had already left. ** It suggests nothing of the kind. ** One person can always be missed or mangled, and ** this person's name demonstrably mangles: the Argentine army indexed his own card as "ARMAND LORENA", born "Rosario de Lerma, SALTA". ** A boy who becomes Armand Lorena on one index can be anything on another. ** SO THE HONEST POSITION IS THAT NOTHING DATES HIS DEPARTURE: ** born Rosario February 1882, son born Cape Town November 1905, ** twenty-three years with no record inside them. ** The live routes are the ones hypothesis 2 already names — ** UK outward passenger lists (BT 27), indexed from 1890 ** — and the consular file behind the 1940 passport. ** And note the archive already reasoned that the South African War shipped some 360,000 horses in, Argentina among the sources, when he was 17 to 20 and a horseman. **

rows.what: Sweep the interior through FamilySearch — done once, and it found the generation above the nest
rows.note: ** This came out of measuring the four departments, and it is worth more than any of the names that measurement failed to turn up. ** ** The archive's Uruguayan baptism layer, uruguay-baptisms-lerena.tsv, is a FINDMYPAST FREE RESULT LIST ** — its own header says **"33 index rows... transcripts are behind findmypast's paywall and were NOT opened"** — giving names, years and parents' **forenames only**. Twenty-two rows: eleven Trinidad, four Montevideo, three San José de Mayo. ** Beside it, free, sit 1,343 exact LERENA records across the same four departments ** with **parents in full** and frequently a **View original document** link. For Trinidad the 608 split roughly half **Catholic Church Records 1726–2000**, half **Civil Registration 1879–2020**, and only a couple from **Uruguay Baptisms 1750–1900** — ** which is the index findmypast was charging to transcribe. ** ** Fair to the earlier work: ** the register does cite Catholic Church Records for particular people, so the collection was known — ** it was used person by person, never swept. ** ** THE JOB: ** take Flores, San José, Florida and Colonia one collection at a time, harvest every exact LERENA with its full parentage, and build the Trinidad kindred **upward**. That is the difference between knowing Bernabé married a Casimira Pelaez and being able to put a generation above either of them — ** which is the only way the Trinidad nest will ever be joined to Sancho, or shown to be a separate family. ** ** RUN ONCE, 17 September 2026, AND IT WORKED THE FIRST TIME. ** Searching **by parent** instead of by person turned up ** MAURICIO LERENA and CASIMIRA MONTAÑO **, a couple with at least seven children across San José de Mayo, Trinidad, Florida, Salto and Montevideo. ** One of them is CIPRIANO LERENA MONTAÑA, and Cipriano is one of the six Trinidad fathers ** — so the archive now has a generation above the nest for the first time. ** Another is CLARA LERENA, b. 1848, d. Montevideo 3 March 1925 certificate 47, which is almost certainly the tree's "Demetria Clara Lerena Montaño" ** — and the record **explains** the compound name, because her mother was Montaño. See data/mauricio-casimira-montano.tsv. ** Graded honestly: Cipriano's card says Image Unavailable, so it is an INDEX and not an act. ** ** The method is proved and the sweep is barely begun — Alejandro Lerena, Emilio Lerena and Alejandro F. Lerena all appear as fathers in the same window and none has been worked. **

rows.what: Mauricio's parents — found. Ramón Lerena of Rosario, and he is NOT Sancho's son
rows.note: ** ANSWERED 17 September 2026, in two searches, and the answer is a SEPARATION. ** ** MAURICIO LERENA, born at COLLA, married Casimira Montaño at San José de Mayo on 3 February 1837 ** — father **Ramón**, mother **María Gonzales** (ark 1:1:F21B-SZ5). And his brother: ** ALEJANDRO LERENA, born at ROSARIO, married Margarita Fernández Álvarez at San José on 16 September 1825 ** — same parents, **Ramón Lerena and María Josefa Gonsales** (ark 1:1:F21Y-JRV). ** That marriage also closes a circuit the archive opened on 14 September: ** the-three-alejandros.tsv had an "Alejandro Lerena of the Trinidad orbit" with **Severa Fernández and a Bárbara Lerena** and could not place him — ** the Fernández is his wife and the Bárbara is his mother-in-law, Bárbara Sotura. ** ** THE STRUCTURE: Ramón Lerena × María Josefa González of Rosario/Colla → Alejandro, Mauricio, Manuel Lorenzo (b.1812 Unión) and Luís Manuel (b.1820) → and TWO OF THE SIX TRINIDAD FATHERS, Bernabé and Cipriano, WHO ARE FIRST COUSINS. ** ** AND THE ANSWER: RAMÓN IS NOT SANCHO'S SON. ** Alejandro married in 1825, so was born about 1800–05, putting Ramón's birth about **1775–85**. Sancho was baptised about 1767 and married in **January 1791**, his first child born 1793. ** A man born in 1775–85 cannot be the son of a man who married in 1791. ** Ramón is Sancho's contemporary, about ten years his junior. ** So there are TWO documented Uruguayan Lerena families, not one. ** See data/ramon-lerena-rosario.tsv.

rows.what: Ramón's origin — his parents are found, his birthplace is not, and that is now the whole question
rows.note: ** This is now the best-defined question in the whole Uruguayan file, and it turns on a single phrase. ** **Ramón Lerena** married **María Josefa González** and was fathering children from about 1800 (Alejandro, b. Rosario) to 1820 (Luís Manuel). ** So the marriage falls about 1795–1810, most likely at ROSARIO in COLONIA or at SAN JOSÉ. ** ** Uruguayan marriage acts state where the groom is NATURAL DE, and that is the whole question. ** **Sancho Llerena was natural de Córdova la Llana.** ** If Ramón is Córdoban too, the two families are brothers or cousins and the surname entered the Banda Oriental ONCE. If Ramón was born in the Banda Oriental, they are two separate arrivals and may not be related at all. ** ** Where to look: ** Uruguay Catholic Church Records 1726–2000 and Uruguay Marriages, free and indexed, searching Ramón Lerena as groom; and the Rosario (Colonia) parish registers, which this archive has never opened. ** And a loose end worth picking up in the same pass: the current tree gives Gabino of Flores as a son of "RAMÓN LLERENA CUBAS and Margarita Leal" — a different wife. Either Ramón married twice, or there are two Ramóns, and the tree may be carrying a version of this same man. ** ** ADVANCED 17 September 2026, and it went one rung FURTHER than asked. ** The marriage was not found; ** Ramón's PARENTS were: SALVADOR GERENA and ANA DE CUBAS **, named on the baptism of his son Manuel Lorenzo at **Unión, Montevideo, 15 November 1812** (ark 1:1:6D7Z-BD56) — ** because Montevideo acts name grandparents as a matter of course. THE IMAGE IS AVAILABLE AND HAS NOT BEEN READ. ** ** That also explains the tree's "Ramón Llerena CUBAS": Cubas is his mother's surname. ** Second time in two days a record has explained a compound name the tree merely carried. ** AND IT SETTLES HALF THE QUESTION: SANCHO AND RAMÓN ARE NOT BROTHERS. ** Sancho's father was **Félix**, Ramón's was **Salvador**. ** They may still be cousins, and the one thing that keeps it worth chasing is the SPELLING: ** both fathers are written **GERENA** in Montevideo acts a year apart — 1811 and 1812. ** A scribal habit of one place and time, not two families choosing the same variant by chance. A resemblance, not evidence. ** ** WHAT REMAINS: read the 1812 act, which may say where Ramón was natural de and close it in one reading. ** ** CLOSED 17 September 2026 by row 140. ** The marriage was never found, and it did not need to be: ** the 1812 act states Ramón is natural de VALDEMORO en CASTILLA LA NUEVA. ** Not Córdoba. The two houses are two Spanish emigrations, and the question this row existed to ask is answered.

rows.what: The 1812 act, read — Ramón is from VALDEMORO, and the two houses are two Spanish arrivals
rows.note: ** READ 17 September 2026, and it closed the question in five words. ** **DGS 007713375, image 02668** — ** which is the film already sitting on this work list as row 5. ** "…hijo legítimo de **RAMON SERENA natural de VALDEMORO en CASTILLA LA NUEVA**, y de María Josefa González **natural de la Ysla de Canarias, LANZAROTE**. Abuelos paternos **Salvador Serena y Ana de Cubas**; id. maternos **Marcial de León González è Ysavel Lorenza**." ** VALDEMORO IS 27 KM SOUTH OF MADRID. SANCHO WAS NATURAL DE CÓRDOVA LA LLANA, IN ANDALUSIA, 500 KM AWAY. ** So the surname entered the Banda Oriental **twice, from opposite ends of Spain** — two emigrations, not one kindred. ** And the Gerena/Gerena coincidence, which this archive flagged as "a reason to look and not a reason to believe", is discharged: the act writes SERENA, and the two men were baptising children at the SAME FONT one year apart. The resemblance was real and it meant nothing. ** ** The act also beat the index nine facts to four: ** the father's birthplace, the mother's birthplace, the real maternal grandmother (**Ysavel Lorenza**, whom the index never named and for whom the child Manuel **Lorenzo** is probably named), and the church — ** the index says "Unión" and the act says the Iglesia Matriz. ** See data/1812-union-act.tsv and /uruguay/.

rows.what: Valdemoro — the place-name is hard, and its registers are not on FamilySearch
rows.note: ** What the 1812 act bought in exchange for closing the join. ** An hour ago Ramón's house had no origin at all; it now has two, both precise. ** ONE: VALDEMORO, in Castilla la Nueva, 27 km south of Madrid. ** **Salvador Serena and Ana de Cubas were married in Spain** and Ramón was baptised there about **1775–85** — ** both findable, because Valdemoro is one parish and not a province. ** FamilySearch holds Spanish diocesan records for Toledo and Madrid; PARES and the Spanish diocesan portals are row 78. ** TWO, AND NOBODY SUSPECTED IT: MARÍA JOSEFA GONZÁLEZ IS A CANARIA, FROM LANZAROTE. ** Her parents are **Marcial de León González** and **Ysavel Lorenza**. ** The Canary Islands fed a migration stream of their own into the River Plate and no part of this archive has ever looked at it. ** ** A CAUTION BEFORE ANYONE SPENDS A WEEK: none of this is Pablo Armando's line. ** It is Ramón's house, which the same act has just proved is NOT Sancho's, and neither house has yet produced a Juan Carlos. ** Work it because it is real and cheap, not because it is his. ** ** TESTED 17 September 2026 AND BLOCKED, with a control. ** FamilySearch's catalogue holds ** exactly ONE item for Valdemoro and it is a CENSUS **; a catalogue search for **church records** there returns ** "No Results Found" **. ** The control is the census: the place resolves and the search works, so the null is about the holdings. FAMILYSEARCH HAS NO VALDEMORO PARISH REGISTERS. ** ** And a warning repeated because it has now misled twice: ** an indexed search for SERENA filtered to "Valdemoro, Madrid, Spain" returns **79 hits and not one of them is Valdemoro** — Madrid city, Toledo, Murcia, Almería, Huesca. ** The place filter silently widens to the province, exactly as it did for Santa Fe. Check the place field on the rows. ** ** THE ROUTE IS DIOCESAN, NOT FILMED: ** Valdemoro is historically **Archdiocese of Toledo**, since 1991 **Diocese of Getafe**, and **PARES** is the state portal. That is row 78 — which until today said only "try PARES and the Spanish diocesan portals" and had no place to try them on. ** It now has one, and a precise target: Ramón's baptism about 1775–85, and the marriage of Salvador Serena and Ana de Cubas before it. **

rows.what: Evidence now reaches the person, and a gate refuses the build if it stops
rows.note: ** The Mazza fault was looked for here and found in a different shape. ** Mazza kept evidence in files its person-builder never read. ** This archive had no person-keyed evidence file AT ALL: ** build-people.py read lerena-register.tsv and relations.tsv and nothing else, so a whole session of records lived on topic pages while the people they were about had pages saying **"No relationships are recorded for this person."** ** AND THE GATE FOUND A PRE-EXISTING ONE ON ITS FIRST RUN, which is the real vindication. ** /people/carlos-lerena-salvanach/ carried that sentence while relations.tsv held **five** edges for him — father Gilberto, mother Julia Salvanach, wives Rosa Maria Eppens and Adela Camiglia, son Avelino Carlos. ** The cause is on his own page: the row was corrected on 14 September from "Retiro baptism" to "información matrimonial", and the rename fixed the register and orphaned every edge. relations.tsv does if not subj: continue — it drops unknown names in silence. ** All five repointed and recovered. ** THE FIX: ** data/person-evidence.tsv (person-keyed, same name convention as relations.tsv); build-people.py reads it and **raises** on an unknown name rather than skipping; the person page renders **What has been read about this person** and no longer prints the false claim when evidence exists. ** THE GATE: ** tools/check-evidence.py, wired into verify.sh and into npm run build so CI runs it. It refuses if a named person is not in the register, if their page does not carry their evidence, if the page still prints the false claim, or if relations.tsv names anyone the register lacks. ** Verified by reintroducing the bug three ways — build stops reading the file, template guard removed, edge repointed at an unknown name — each exits 1. **

rows.what: Order the Royal Marines attestation of John Walker Brayley, ADM 157/197/182

This archive has its John Walker Brayley born **1845 at St Paul's, London** — which is Middlesex — and has already logged that his death index gives **age 53 in the December quarter of 1900, implying about 1847: a two-year gap left open**. Aged 18 in 1861 implies about 1843. **Three sources, three different years.** An attestation paper states date and place of birth outright and would settle it. **Not asserted to be him** — that is what the document is for.

rows.what: Decide whether to buy ADM 188/195/140021, the Northam William Taylor
rows.note: **Settled 17 September 2026. David signed the archive into a TNA account and ordered the record himself; it was free.** And it does more than nail the rejection down — it **replaces the argument**. The rejection had rested on a census age. The document gives two harder reasons. **First, the form asks for 'Names in full' and the answer is plain 'William Taylor'** — ours is William **John** Taylor, and the Navy had no reason to drop a middle name it had just asked for. **Second, and it is conclusive: on census night, 5 April 1891, this man was borne on HMS Impregnable at Devonport** (joined 20 May 1890, left 4 October 1892) **while William John Taylor was enumerated at home in Northam, aged 20.** One man cannot be in two places on one night. **Two men, proved.** The near miss is closed rather than merely argued.

rows.what: Cost the merchant crew lists before starting them
rows.note: If the Taylor men went to sea it was **not the Royal Navy** — that is now a tested null. The merchant service remains open, but **crew lists are indexed by SHIP, not by man**, so there is no name search to run. A Taylor family of **Appledore**, in Northam parish, appears on the **Ulelia** (ON 74429) — T Taylor mate b.1846, J W Taylor master b.1888, T G Taylor b.1893, previous ship **Annie of Bideford** — **joined to this family by nothing at all**. Work out what a ship-by-ship search would actually cost in hours before committing to it. ** COSTED AND CLOSED 20 September 2026 — it costs nothing, because it must not be started. ** **The 1891 census already answered it**, and had been in this archive since 16 September: **William John, 20, is a CAB DRIVER** like his father; **Horace Archibald, 19, is a FOOTMAN in domestic service**. Neither went to sea, which also gives the ADM 188 null its reason. For the record, the search would have meant **several thousand annual agreements across a hundred-odd Bideford and Appledore vessels, held in three institutions** — and it could not have been done by name in any case, because **no central register of merchant seamen survives between 1857 and 1918**, which is exactly when either man would have sailed. See /taylor/.

Anything wider goes to image-library@nationalarchives.gov.uk. Note also that **download links expire 30 days from the order**, so anything wanted long-term must be read and transcribed inside that window — ADM 188/195/140021 was ordered 17 September 2026.

That reaches the generation above the wall from records that should exist. Also asks for a **late birth inscription** (he held an Argentine passport and was enrolled in 1908; both needed proof of birth, and no baptism exists) and, failing everything, a **certificado negativo** — which for this archive is a document, not a disappointment. **Registro Civil, San Luis 2950, CP 3000, Santa Fe** (verified on the province's own site). rows.what: Add GONZALEZ LERENA to the compound-surname sweep
rows.note: A full-text hit turned up **'Don Juan Carlos González Lerena'** in the Montevideo dispensations, 8 November 1920. He is not ours. But **González Lerena appears in neither compound-surname-sweep.tsv nor lerena-lerena-compound-test.tsv**, so the compound sweep is incomplete by at least one variant — and compound forms are how this surname hides. ** SWEPT 20 September 2026, and it was not one variant — it was a family. ** **'Gonzalez Lerena' exact returns 52 records**, headed by **ESTEFANÍA LERENA, wife of Servando González**, with at least six children across San José, Montevideo and Colonia, 1854–1931. **None of it was in either compound file.** She is attached to nothing and is recorded unplaced. It also finishes the false positive: **Juan Carlos González Lerena, b. 1899**, married Concepción Petrona Urbano Orio in 1922, son of Leopoldo — Estefanía's grandson, and seventeen years younger than Pablo Armando. See /uruguay/.

rows.what: Place the Santa Fe city Lerenas — Casimiro Lerena and Amelia Lepiani

Recorded unplaced; test it, do not adopt it. ** TESTED 20 September 2026, and it is not a Santa Fe household. ** **Casimiro Lerena and Amelia Lepiani** — indexed once as **Lapriani** — have **Armando Lerena** in the Santa Fe church records **and Ventura Amelia Argentina Lerena in the Entre Ríos records**. So the family is **littoral, across two provinces**, and Entre Ríos is also where Gilberto and Julia Salvañach's 1885 child sits — **the province is worth mapping in its own right.** **Attached to Pablo Armando by nothing whatever.** The only thing that ever recommended this household was the forename **Armando**, which is not evidence, and it has not been treated as any.

And **Legal Notices B 18373 (24 Oct 1997, p.165)**, **ABSA Bank Beperk v Lerena** in the Witwatersrand Local Division — **the snippet cuts off before the forenames**, so which Lerena is unknown. rows.what: Rosario, in Colonia — the one Uruguayan department still unaccounted for
rows.note: The last remainder of row 120. Three of the four departments measured there resolved to the children of **one couple, Mauricio Lerena and Casimira Montaño**, spreading across the interior in a single generation — San José de Mayo, Trinidad in Flores, and Florida, with Salto and Montevideo besides. **Colonia did not.** It holds **189 exact LERENA records** and has no dedicated study, only passing mentions. And the standing warning applies to it hardest: the tree's Gabino of Flores is given as a son of **Ramón Llerena Cubas and Margarita Leal — not Sancho's line** — so the interior may hold a different Lerena family entirely, and Colonia is where that would show. Needs a FamilySearch session. ** PART-ANSWERED 20 September 2026, and the method was the problem. ** **Maria Bernarda González Lerena married at Campana, Colonia in 1931** — so part of Colonia's Lerena presence is a **compound** family that an exact-surname count cannot see. **The 189 figure was measured by exact surname and therefore under-counts.** Before anyone concludes Colonia is thin, re-measure it including compound forms. ** CLOSED 20 September 2026, AND THE ROW'S PREMISE WAS WRONG - my own row, logged as a correction. ** **Rosario-Colla was never unaccounted for: it is where the family came from.** The archive's own notes already read **Ramón Lerena × María Josefa González, of Rosario / Colla, fathering children c.1800-1820** and **from Rosario-Colla across San José, Flores, Florida, Salto** — and the **1837 San José marriage gives Mauricio's birthplace as COLLA outright**. What was genuinely missing was that **none of them were people here**: Mauricio, his father Ramón of Colla, his mother María Josefa González and his wife Casimira Montaño have now been added to the register with their edges, from ark 1:1:F21B-SZ5, tiered **INDEXED not image-read**. Also new: **Vitalino Lerena, born San Pedro, COLONIA in 1870**, son of Vitalino Lerena and Andrea Echeverry — **a documented link between Colonia and the Trinidad/Flores kindred.**

rows.what: Re-run any exact-forename null recorded against a two-forename person
rows.note: **133 of the 278 people in this register carry two or more forenames** — very nearly half — and FamilySearch's exact forename search matches the **whole given-name string**, so an exact search on the first forename alone would never have found them. **Any null recorded that way is unsafe.** None could be identified by grep, because the searches were written down in prose without naming the parameter, **which is the lesson underneath this row: record the query, not just the answer.** Re-run suspects in the safe shape — fuzzy forename, exact surname — which does match per token. **RUN 21 September 2026, and it found something better than a bad null.** The archive's own blast-radius note says no affected null could be identified by grep, because the searches were written in prose without naming the parameter — so the sharpest available version was run instead: the CENTRAL null, re-done in the fuzzy-forename / exact-surname shape. **Fuzzy 'Juan' + exact LERENA returns 29 distinct given-name forms**, including *Juan Carlos Esteban Lerena*, *Juan a. Lerena* and *Juan P. Lerena* — the initial and three-forename shapes a whole-string exact match cannot reach, which is exactly what the trap predicted. None is the father: the Esteban man married in 1932. **But the re-run falsified two published zeroes** — see corrections.tsv. Juan Carlos Lerena is now an indexed person, as the father on his own son's military record.

rows.what: Read the 1877 Gilberto–Salvañach marriage image — it may document his parents
rows.note: Found while running a control. Marriage of **Gilberto Lerena and Julia Salvañach, 11 August 1877, San Francisco de Asís, Ciudad Vieja, Montevideo**. Index ark **1:1:X9PV-HKCR**; **image ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-N74V-N**. The index gives the bride's parents-in-law — Gilberto's parents — as **'Luís Lenguas' and 'Justiniana Lenguas'**, almost certainly a machine garble of **Luis LERENA and Justiniana LENGUAS**, which is exactly the couple this archive assigns him **at tree tier only**. rows.what: drift.py's catch is verified now, and three ledger pages had made it toothless
rows.note: **The blind spot it had was real and is fixed**: drift.py read only the .astro **sources**, so it could see a finding a page had **typed** and was blind to one a page **rendered**. That put it in direct conflict with check-onsite.py, which requires every data file to be imported by a page — onsite said **render it**, drift said **no page says it**, and drift was wrong every time. It now reads the built pages, excluding **/people/, /register/, /who/ and /search/**, which re-print the whole register and would make any finding pass trivially. **What is NOT verified:** deleting the /uruguay/ section that carries the Mauricio finding did **not** make the check report it again, even though no other non-dump page and no .astro source holds those words. **So the fix is sound but the catch is unproven, and a gate whose catch is unproven is a gate nobody should trust.** Find out why — most likely the rarest-word selection shifts as the corpus grows. ** VERIFIED BOTH WAYS, 20 September 2026 - and my own test was broken first. ** The first attempt rebuilt with npm run build >/dev/null 2>&1 and **never checked the exit code** — the very trap verify.sh carries a warning about. Read off **film 008166435, image 02850**: **Pedro Alberto Ysabelino Lerena, born 16 March 1852**, baptised at the Aguada on **21 November 1852** — not 1896 — *libro 1.º de Bautismos, folio 135*, **godparents Pedro Antonio Lerena and Vicenta Vega**, his own uncle and aunt, and a man born in 1793 who could not stand at a font in 1896. He is the **Alberto** who died at Montevideo on 1 March 1921. The same opening carries **Josefa's own baptism**, which gives her a day at last: **born 10 February 1851**, and christened **Josefina**. From the indexes: **Juan Arturo born 16 February 1861**, **Mercedes Micaela born 8 May 1863** — with Sancho and María Fernández named as her grandparents, a **third** independent attestation of that parentage — and **María Adelina**, who married **Carlos Alberto Fein** and died in 1946. The tell that catches this trap is cheap: **two children of one couple indexed with the same birth date**. See /method/ and data/1852-aguada-union-certificates.tsv.

rows.note: **A woman this archive had written off is ours, and she has eight brothers and sisters.** On 14 September **Zelmira Carlota Lerena Larriera**, born in the Departamento de San José on 4 November 1880, was tested and closed: *"she is NOT ours"*. The row named the one thing that would overturn it — who her father **Alberto Lerena** was — guessed **Alberto Octavio Lerena Lenguas**, and refused to draw the line on a forename and an age. **It is the other grandfather.** Alberto's Montevideo death act No. 246 of 2 March 1921 names his wife **María Inés Larriera** and his parents **Avelino Lerena and Ambrosia Treibel** — so her father is **Pedro Alberto Ysabelino Lerena Traibel** of the Aguada, and Zelmira is a **great-granddaughter of Sancho**. Asking for Alberto and María Inés as a *pair* then returned a whole household born in San José between 1879 and 1898. **And the image was opened rather than left as an errand**, which is where the real find was: the act counts **nueve hijos** and names them, so there is a **ninth child** — *Eleiza* or *Eloiza*, read at three times magnification and still not securely read — whom no index has matched. **Eight index entries look like eight confirmations and are one indexing project; one death act is a different mouth.** See /uruguay/ and data/alberto-lerena-larriera.tsv.
